clue.text: Spoil the quality of some cricket in tricksy surroundings

indicators.note: the cricket term sits in the middle of the other word, which wraps round it
surroundings says the word for tricksy forms the outside casing here

parts.note: tricksy means impish, mischievous
an over is a set of six balls in cricket, so a portion of the game

explanation.surface: A grumble that some tricky setting has ruined the standard of a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'surroundings' together signal the container. 'the quality of' belongs to the definition: to spoil the quality of something is to make it poorer.
explanation.definitionFit: To impoverish land or a thing is to degrade it, reduce its richness, so spoil is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Very short distance from home to church

parts.note: at home means in

explanation.surface: A short walk: the house sits right beside the church.
explanation.definitionFit: An inch is a tiny unit of length, used figuratively for any very small distance.

clue.text: Long to meet Lady Bagheera?

parts.note: to long for something is to pant for it
her is the pronoun for a woman, a lady

explanation.surface: Someone yearning to be introduced to an aristocratic lady.
explanation.walkthrough: Bagheera is the black leopard in Kipling's The Jungle Book; the question mark marks him as an example of the big cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagheera in The Jungle Book is a black leopard, commonly called a black panther, so he exemplifies the animal.

clue.text: Abusive language bursts out in private

indicators.note: bursts suggests the following words break apart and scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: Swearing that erupts behind closed doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bursts' looks like part of 'bursts out', but 'out' is fodder: OUT IN PRIVATE, twelve letters, is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Vituperation is bitter, abusive criticism or invective, which is abusive language.

clue.text: Shown in colour, organ set upright

indicators.note: shown in says the organ word appears inside the colour word

parts.note: red is a colour
the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: An organ, painted a bright hue, is erected.
explanation.definitionFit: Reared means raised up on end, as a horse rears, so stood or set upright.

clue.text: Expel from university and bang up

explanation.surface: A student thrown out of college and then jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: To be sent down is British university slang for being expelled; to send down is also to jail someone, and 'bang up' is British slang for imprisoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a university expels by sending a student down, and a judge sends a criminal down to prison.

clue.text: In the current circumstances, I will have to board a ship

indicators.note: to board is to get on a ship, so the single letter goes inside the ship's letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Under present conditions, I shall have to embark on a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's 'a' is taken as it stands; 'will have' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: As is means in the present state, without changes, so in the current circumstances.

clue.text: One plant being pulled up by Japanese military

indicators.note: in a down entry pulling up reads the whole run from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
the arum is a plant, the lily family's cuckoo-pint
as means being, in the sense of since

explanation.surface: A single shrub is uprooted by soldiers from Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled up' turns IARUMAS round to give the answer; 'by' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: The samurai were the hereditary military class of feudal Japan.

clue.text: Searching through what's been discarded ——in other words, getting one's own back

parts.note: sc, short for the Latin scilicet, means namely, in other words
avenging is taking revenge, getting one's own back

explanation.surface: A rummager in the rubbish, said to be settling a score.
explanation.walkthrough: SC (scilicet) is a dictionary abbreviation meaning 'namely', the kind of note that introduces a restatement.
explanation.definitionFit: To scavenge is to search through refuse for anything usable.

clue.text: Check carton isn't damaged

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning to inspect a box that is not broken.
explanation.definitionFit: A check is a restraint or limit on something, the same sense as a constraint.

clue.text: Excerpt from poem "Marmion" featured in book

indicators.note: Excerpt from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A passage from Scott's poem Marmion appearing in a volume.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'featured in book' as the definition, but EMMA is the book itself, Jane Austen's novel; 'featured in' is linking. Marmion is a poem by Walter Scott.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is the title of Jane Austen's 1815 novel, so it names a book.

clue.text: Two nuns rig pad, working — and working properly

indicators.note: working implies the letters are being worked over, kneaded into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: two of the word nun side by side

explanation.surface: A couple of sisters equip a launch pad that is now operational.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' is the anagram signal, and 'working properly' (sharing a word but separate) is the definition after 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Up and running is an idiom for something functioning as intended, working properly.

clue.text: Pastor encourages English weed

parts.note: a pastor is a shepherd of his flock
spurs means urges on, encourages

explanation.surface: A minister urges on an Englishman, or else a garden plant gets mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Shepherd's purse is a common white-flowered weed of the cabbage family.

clue.text: Bird giving dirty look when love leaves to bounce back inside

indicators.note: inside places the shortened echo word within the frowning word

parts.note: a scowl is a dirty look

indicators.note: leaves means the zero goes away from the echo word

parts.note: to re-echo is to bounce back as an echo does
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A bird shoots a filthy glare when a sweetheart walks out, only to rebound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' signals the removal of love's letter and 'inside' the container; to re-echo is to echo again. 'giving' and 'when' are linking.
explanation.definitionFit: The screech owl is a bird, the name for the barn owl in Britain and small American owls.

clue.text: Copper encounters unusual poison

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
rare means unusual

explanation.surface: A policeman comes across a strange toxin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman, but here it is the metal; 'encounters' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Curare is a South American plant poison once used on arrow tips.

clue.text: Pretentious pen and ruler

parts.note: a pen is a female swan
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A fancy fountain pen and a measuring ruler on a desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' and 'ruler' suggest stationery, but a pen is a female swan and the ruler a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Swanking means showing off, behaving ostentatiously, which is pretentious.

clue.text: Place that might calm you down

parts.note: stead means place, as in 'in his stead'
yon is an old word for that, over there

explanation.surface: A soothing location where one can relax.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady on! is a British exclamation telling someone to calm down or slow up.

clue.text: Sloth, perhaps, apparent in garden beside gallery

parts.note: Eden is the biblical garden
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: Laziness appears in a park next to a museum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sloth' reads as idleness but is the animal; 'apparent in' and 'beside' are linking. The Tate is a group of British art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentates are toothless mammals, an old order that includes sloths, so a sloth is an example.

clue.text: Receive electric shock treatment? That's serious

parts.note: to earn is to receive as pay
EST stands for electroshock therapy

explanation.surface: A question about getting zapped as therapy, followed by a grave reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' is linking, leading to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means serious in intention, sincere and grave.

clue.text: Continue slowly, and arrive at the Lizard

explanation.surface: Plod on and reach the Lizard, Cornwall's southern tip.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lizard is a peninsula in Cornwall, but here it is the animal; 'and arrive at the' only links the senses.
explanation.definitionFit: To drag on is to go on tediously; a dragon such as the Komodo is a large lizard.

clue.text: In great shape, showing determination

indicators.note: putting letters into a new shape signals a rearrangement of them

explanation.surface: Being very fit shows resolve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In great shape' reads as 'fit', but IN GREAT is fodder and 'shape' the anagram signal; 'showing' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Granite figuratively means unyielding firmness of will, as in granite-like resolve.

clue.text: Going up river valley to obscure spot above the ground

indicators.note: in a down entry going up reads the run from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a ria is a drowned river valley
to dim is to obscure

explanation.surface: Climbing a valley to hide a vantage point high up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going up' turns RIADIM round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Midair is the space above the ground, a point not touching anything.

clue.text: Levy sees soldiers (ten) being added to company

indicators.note: being added to puts the soldiers and ten after the company word

parts.note: a corporation is a company
TA is the Territorial Army, British reserve soldiers
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: A tax collector sees ten troops joining a firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sees' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation tax is the British tax levied on company profits.

clue.text: One parliamentarian's mischievous children

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
MP is a member of parliament; the possessive gives the S

explanation.surface: A politician's naughty offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Imps are mischievous children, little devils.

clue.text: Exposed, begin to crack

explanation.surface: Something laid bare starts to fracture.
explanation.definitionFit: Open means uncovered, exposed; to open a case or bottle is to crack it, begin it.

clue.text: Brit says "I'm troubled by a sensual addiction"

indicators.note: troubled letters are disturbed, stirred up into another order

explanation.surface: A Briton confesses distress at a craving for pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Sybaritism is devotion to luxury and pleasure, after the luxurious ancient city of Sybaris.

clue.text: Dead on time? No!

explanation.surface: A question whether someone is precisely punctual, answered in the negative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead on time' reads as one phrase, but 'Dead' is one definition and 'on time? No!' the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Late means deceased, as in 'the late king', and also means not punctual.

clue.text: Through entrance, for going on

indicators.note: through says the word for in favour of passes into the entrance word

parts.note: ingress means entrance, the way in
pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: Going in by the doorway, for a passage.
explanation.definitionFit: In progress means under way, happening now.
